summary: The text discusses the challenges of teaching traditional scholarly methods in the study of women writers, particularly in relation to revising the canon. To address this, a unique pedagogical approach was developed, where students worked on a collaborative project about a neglected 18th-century writer, Elizabeth Griffith. This approach aimed to provide students with hands-on experience and master the literature quickly, while minimizing artificial aspects of traditional courses. The project also served as a teaching tool to educate students about the importance of using reliable sources and handling outdated information, specifically in the context of the exclusion of a writer (likely D.H. Lawrence's wife) from the literary canon.
